Engineering Notebook

Hi, I am Ishan Gupta. This site is a candid, first-person record of my software projects, systems engineering experiments, and architecture decisions.

MAVIS Architecture Series

An engineering deep-dive series on designing and building MAVIS (My Awesome Virtual Intelligence Suite) — a local-first, self-modifying personal assistant inspired by JARVIS. These posts discuss the technical design and choices on using DAGs, synthesizing tools on-the-fly, enforcing OS policy gates, managing multi-tier memory, and building compute-bounded autonomous reflection.

Part 0 Oct 21, 2026

MAVIS Part 0 — Overview & Motivation: Personal Agents Can Be Cool

Why build another personal assistant? To experiment on how personal assistants can both be flexible and proactive.

Part 1 Oct 21, 2026

MAVIS Part 1 — Planning & Dynamic Tooling: Feedforward DAGs, ToolBuilder and AgentBuilder

Why MAVIS rejects free-form conversational ReAct loops in favor of acyclic Directed Acyclic Graphs, and how ToolBuilder and AgentBuilder synthesize self-tested tools and agents.

Part 2 Oct 21, 2026

MAVIS Part 2 — Security & Observability: Policy Gates and Metrics Dashboard

How do you give an AI assistant system access without handing over full control? How do you observe the different parts of the system?

Part 3 Oct 21, 2026

MAVIS Part 3 — Memory Architecture: 3 Tiers, Discrete Labels, and Topic-based Knowledge Graphs

How MAVIS manages context across sessions without catastrophic forgetting: three cognitive tiers, verified promotion criteria, and topic-subscribed Neo4j knowledge graphs.

Part 4 Oct 21, 2026

MAVIS Part 4 — Semantic Caching: Plan vs. Result Reuse

How MAVIS cuts latency and token costs: SQLite vector caching, tiered similarity thresholds, separating plan reuse from result TTLs, and deterministic regex pre-filters.

Part 5 Oct 21, 2026

MAVIS Part 5 — Autonomous Reflection: Curiosity, Rut Detection, and Gated Beliefs

Can an AI agent explore on its own and learn? Designing an adversarial generator-critic loop under the principle: exploration is good, but it should be worthwhile.

Part 6 Coming Soon

MAVIS Part 6 — Evaluation: Designing MAVIS-Bench for Evaluation

Why existing benchmarks fail to evaluate MAVIS, and how MAVIS-Bench scores autonomy across 5 orthogonal axes: proactivity, completeness, resilience, safety, and efficiency. (Currently in progress).
